title: OCDS contracts ingestion + explainer module (entity-level, PII-screened)
context: Public contracts data, published under the Open Contracting Data Standard (OCDS), must be ingested with per-publisher license verification (OCDS is a format, not a license) and the PII entity-vs-person screen applied before any contracts explainer is generated. Contracts explainers describe buyers, supplier entities, values, and categories — entity-level only, with no allegations of impropriety for any named vendor or official. This module extends the pipeline to the contracts domain. Depends on pii-008 and template-010.
objective: Implement the OCDS contracts ingestion and explainer module that ingests OCDS releases (with per-publisher license verification), normalizes to the Contract data model, applies the PII entity-vs-person screen, and generates contracts explainers describing buyers, supplier entities, values, and categories at entity-level only — with no allegations of impropriety — passing the neutrality lint, reconciliation gate, and citation-coverage gate before review.
acceptanceCriteria: Ingests OCDS releases with per-publisher license verification (not blanket OCDS format assumption); only license-clean sources are enabled
Normalizes OCDS data to the Contract data model (task 005): ocid, sourceId, jurisdiction, buyer, supplierEntity, supplierIsEntity, value, currency, awardDate, category, status
PII entity-vs-person screen (task 008) applied; entity-level output only; private-individual personal data redacted or withheld
Generated contracts explainers describe buyers, supplier entities, values, and categories — no allegations of impropriety, fraud, or corruption against any named vendor or official
Figures reconcile; citations resolve to snapshot line items; neutrality lint passes
Public-finance expert sign-off recorded for contracts content; PR merged with green CI and maintainer plus neutrality reviewer review passed
output: A merged PR containing the OCDS contracts ingestion and explainer module: per-publisher license verification, Contract data model normalization, PII screening, and entity-level-only neutrality-passing contracts explainer generation — all behind the reconciliation and citation-coverage gates.
